title: Phase 0 context-economy measurement: do fan-out fixed overhead and retries dominate amplification?
summary: Hypothesis: per-worker input-token amplification in orchestrator runs is dominated by fixed fan-out overhead (each worker re-reading the same prompt scaffold and context) and by retries/checkpoint resumes, rather than by task-specific work. Method: ran the deterministic, privacy-safe `agent-os orchestrate context-economy` harness read-only over .agent-local/orchestrator/runs (20 runs, 653 exact-usage calls), reporting aggregates only (no prompt or transcript text). Outcome: positive for fan-out, only partly for retries. Fixed fan-out overhead is 253.4M of 255.8M worker input tokens (share 0.9905), so task-specific input is about 1%; pooled amplification is 104.8x and the median worker role (implementer/repairer/test_author) sees 141-189x, while reviewers sit at 11.7x. Retries/repeat attempts account for 47.7M tokens (about 19% of worker input; 26 retries, 63 escalations, 15 fallbacks) and checkpoint-resume overhead is 17.2% of run input in the runs that resumed, so retries and resumes are material but secondary. Long sessions do not enlarge later calls (per-node last/first input median 0.78 and 0.43) but cumulative input per run grows superlinearly in most runs (exponent up to 1.88). Interpretation: the fixed per-worker context is the main lever for IMP-0018 and most of it is cache reads (median cache-read share 0.84), so savings depend on trimming scaffold size and worker count rather than on fewer retries. Caveat: the overhead share is a model-based upper bound and the amplification denominator is a characters/4 estimate. See EVR-0018.
